lag_observations.assumption: fix round 3, item 6 (unresolved): these three observed lags (3, 6, 15 days) all fit comfortably within the 90-day forward pad, and none of the three or four documented action types checked here has ever been observed to exceed it. This is NOT proof that every action type's governing-to-process lag stays under 90 days -- no dividend or other action exceeding 90 days has been found OR searched for exhaustively, and Alpaca's own documentation does not state a maximum lag or guarantee upcoming-action announcement availability at all (an empty response cannot establish comprehensive absence of an upcoming action). The 90-day pad remains a documented, evidence-backed but unproven assumption, not an established bound.

claim_boundary: Confirms that the live Alpaca source returns and normalizes these historical windows correctly (type and governing date), that the guard's original today..next_session fetch window was too narrow to reliably observe a real dividend (Alpaca's endpoint filters by process/payable date, not the ex_date this guard's evaluate_guard logic checks against), and the exact 3-day governing-to-process lag for this specific AAPL dividend (see raw_record_lag row and lag_observations above -- corrects this file's own earlier, unmeasured '1-3 weeks' claim). It does NOT establish a maximum lag bound for any action type (see lag_observations.assumption), does not exercise the guard inside a running paper trial end-to-end, a multi-day overnight resume against the live endpoint, the refresh cadence against the endpoint's rate limits, the raw_data=True/data_quality=all/unmapped-bucket-type parsing path introduced in fix round 3 (covered instead by tests/test_adaptive_paper_corporate_actions.py's faked-HTTP-response tests, not this native check), or action types other than forward split and cash dividend.
